item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q008_v1_atp_synthase_bulge_classification","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, the V1 ATP synthase A-subunit bulge domain is not merged into the older barrel-sandwich-hybrid superfamilies. It is placed as its own superfamily, b.84.5 \"V1 ATP synthase A subunit, bulge domain-like\" (SUNID 310577), within fold b.84 \"Barrel-sandwich hybrid\" (SUNID 51229) and class b \"All beta proteins\" (SUNID 48724). Its family is b.84.5.1 (SUNID 310616), with protein-level entries for both V1 ATP synthase A subunit, bulge domain (SUNID 310706) and A1 ATP synthase A subunit, bulge domain (SUNID 310707). The fold b.84 also contains separate sibling superfamilies b.84.1 Single hybrid motif, b.84.2 Rudiment single hybrid motif, b.84.3 Duplicated hybrid motif, and b.84.4 Ribosomal L27 protein-like. The reason for the separate classification is that the bulge domain shares the barrel-sandwich-hybrid fold architecture, described by SCOPe as a sandwich of half-barrel-shaped beta-sheets, but SCOPe does not treat that fold-level similarity as enough to place it in any of those other superfamilies. The evolutionary claim is therefore scoped: homology is implied within b.84.5, and more tightly within family b.84.5.1, but the parent fold b.84 explicitly does not imply homology above the superfamily level. Thus b.84.5 says the V/A-type ATP synthase A-subunit bulge domains are probably evolutionarily related to each other, not that they are homologous to every barrel-sandwich-hybrid protein. Function transfer and template choice should respect that boundary: ATP-synthase A-subunit bulge function and evolutionary annotation should not be transferred to b.84.1-b.84.4 merely from the shared fold, and b.84.1-b.84.4 representatives are fold/topology analogs at best, not homologous templates for the bulge-domain superfamily. For representative structural examples, use domains actually classified as b.84.5.1, such as d1vdza2, d3a5ca3, or d3j9ta3, with their SCOPe domain boundaries rather than whole-chain or sibling-superfamily representatives. SCOPe also links the b.84.5 superfamily annotation to PubMed 19893485, but that literature xref should be treated as supporting context for the SCOPe placement rather than a license to transfer function outside the superfamily.","evidence_used":["/api/v1","/api/v1/","/api/v1/openapi.yaml","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=bulge&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=V1%20ATP%20synthase%20A%20subunit%20bulge&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=barrel-sandwich-hybrid&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310577","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310577/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310577/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51229/children?limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51229/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51229/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310577/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310616/children?limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310616","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310616/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310616/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/domains?sccs_prefix=b.84.5&limit=20"]}]}
